profile.documented: A chat model documented for text, tools, and structured JSON output, with no reasoning mode and an 8192-token runtime context. It documents 23 languages including English, Ukrainian, Arabic, Chinese, French, German, and Russian, and the run configuration notes that its packaged system message identifies it as Aya while marking its tool use as not documented. Sampling for the run used temperature 0.3.
profile.role_in_run: HOME-01 (Multilingual customer message understanding) was designed around this model. That test asks for a strict JSON record of intent, urgency, entity identifiers, date, amount, and language for customer messages across several languages.

overall.rating_basis: Mean semantic quality 0.855 across 6 scored tests, home-test quality 0.858, and an OK rate of 30.7 percent combine to a rating of 7.5.

home_test.title: Multilingual customer message understanding
home_test.analysis: This was the model's strongest assignment in format discipline: all 24 cases ran and 7 were fully correct, with no fenced or malformed outputs at all. Every one of the 17 misses was a field-level error, almost always a single wrong field such as urgency graded high instead of medium while intent, entities, date, and language were right. The pattern shows a model that understood the multilingual inputs and the output contract but resolved borderline urgency judgments differently from the reference. For a classification-style task scored leniently per field, that is a solid result.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The answer was semantically right but wrapped in a code fence the contract forbids.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On routing, extraction, and RAG cases the model produced fully correct JSON and then surrounded it with triple backticks.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Any pipeline that parses the response strictly will reject correct answers, so a fence-stripping step is mandatory with this model.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: Valid JSON with one or more fields differing from the reference.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On its home multilingual test, 17 of 24 cases missed exactly one field, typically urgency graded high instead of medium with everything else right.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Downstream ticket handling that trusts the urgency field will mis-prioritize a meaningful share of messages.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The response hit the token limit before finishing.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On safety cases the model gave the correct verdict first and then rambled into unrelated tutor-style text until the token budget ran out.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Unbounded chatter after the answer wastes tokens and risks burying the verdict for simple parsers.

strengths: Semantic content is consistently good when format is ignored: mean quality 0.855 across 6 scored tests, with no scored test below 0.800.
Followed a strict bare-JSON contract perfectly on its home test, with 24 of 24 outputs parseable and zero fence violations.
Safety labeling was reliable at 11 of 16 exact matches with quality 0.875, showing sound judgment on non-operational requests.
Routing decisions were right on all 20 attempted support cases, indicating solid comprehension of policy-style prompts.
weaknesses: Habitually wraps JSON in code fences on away tests: 32 fenced responses drove strict credit to zero on routing and extraction tasks.
Urgency grading on the home test disagreed with the reference in 17 of 24 cases, usually one step too high.
Tends to append unrelated explanatory text after finishing safety verdicts, which exhausted the token budget in 4 cases.
Math answers show correct arithmetic but ignore the required answer format, losing strict credit on all 4 affected cases.
use_when: Multilingual support-message classification where output is parsed leniently per field (HOME-01 style).
Support-request routing where a fence-stripping post step normalizes the JSON first (HOME-16 style).
Safety triage labeling of user messages with a strict parser backed by a lenient fallback (HOME-08 style).
Template-style extraction from long texts where near-miss fields are acceptable and reviewed (HOME-12 style).
avoid_when: Strict machine-to-machine JSON pipelines with no tolerance for code fences or extra prose.
Priority or urgency assignment that must match a reference rubric exactly, since grades skew high.
Token-budget-sensitive serving where trailing chatter after the answer costs real money.
Contexts above 8192 tokens, which the runtime cannot serve for this model at all.
hardware_fit: Cold load took 4.3 seconds with the model fully on the GPU, first token arrived in 0.19 seconds, and sustained generation ran at 70.2 tokens per second. That is comfortably fast for interactive chat and classification work on this card. The practical limit is the 8192-token runtime context, which ruled out five long-context tests regardless of speed.
bottom_line: Aya-expanse:8b is the run's multilingual understanding specialist: strong content quality everywhere it ran, held back almost entirely by code fences and minor grading disagreements rather than comprehension failures. Pair it with a lenient parser and it is a dependable classifier and router; feed it to a strict parser unmodified and much of its good work will be rejected.

For cross-lingual search over a few hundred documents, this is a strong result.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The ranking was usable but ordered below the reference ordering.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: The top returned document was relevant in every one of these 21 cases, but a lower-graded document outranked the reference order, so graded metrics assigned partial credit between 0.689 and 1.0.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Top-1 relevance stays intact, but any evaluation or display that depends on exact graded ordering will understate how good the retrieval actually is.

strengths: Top-rank relevance was perfect: a relevant document came first on all 40 cross-lingual and all 30 English queries.
Graded quality of 0.923 cross-lingual and 0.955 English shows the ordering is close to reference even when not exact.
With only two scored tests and both above 0.92, there is no weak area in the retrieval role it was built for.
Deterministic scoring with no format layer at all: nothing was lost to output-contract mistakes.
weaknesses: Secondary-document ordering drifts from the reference in 21 of 70 queries, costing partial graded credit.
Only retrieval was measured, so no conclusion is possible about any other task family.
As an embedding model it cannot answer, explain, or cite anything on its own; a generator is still required downstream.
use_when: Cross-lingual document search where the first result must be relevant (HOME-02 style).
English passage retrieval feeding a generator in a search pipeline (HOME-11 style).
Recall-oriented candidate generation where top-10 coverage matters more than exact ordering.
avoid_when: Any task requiring generated text, answers, or citations, which an embedding model cannot produce.
Evaluations scored on exact graded ordering without tolerance for near-equivalent rankings.
Vision, tool-use, or reasoning workloads, which are outside its documented capability.
hardware_fit: Cold load took 1.4 seconds with the model fully on the GPU, and embedding batches ran without pressure on this card. Retrieval work is the lightest workload in the run: no token generation, no long contexts, no offload. For a search pipeline on this hardware, embedding throughput is effectively a non-issue.
bottom_line: Bge-m3:latest did exactly one job in this run, retrieval, and did it at 0.923 to 0.955 quality with perfect top-1 relevance on all 70 queries. It is the highest-rated model in this group at 8.9, with the honest caveat that the rating rests on retrieval alone.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The response contained no JSON structure the scorer could extract.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On all 16 home RAG cases and 6 more elsewhere, the model answered in full prose sentences with no JSON envelope and no citation list.
failure_analysis.example_quote: The discount for energy-efficient models during the spring sale is 15%. This information is found in Document D5, which is effective on 2026-07-01 and outlines the spring sale promotion.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: RAG answers without citations cannot be verified, so the whole response is unusable for grounded question answering.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: Valid JSON with one or more fields differing from the reference.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On multilingual classification the model got intent and entities right but slipped a date by years or an urgency grade, as in the 2023 date below.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: A wrong date or urgency in an otherwise perfect record silently corrupts downstream handling.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The response hit the token limit before finishing.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On safety cases the model wrote full formal letters instead of a verdict, running past the token budget in 11 of 16 attempts.
failure_analysis.example_quote: Subject: Request for Maintenance: Leaking Tap in the Kitchen
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Verbose roleplay in place of a classification verdict wastes the entire token budget and yields no usable label.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The model made no tool call on a case that required one.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On single-turn function calling it refused 10 of 15 scored cases outright, claiming it had no tools to convert currency.
failure_analysis.example_quote: I'm sorry, I am unable to complete this request as I do not have the necessary tools to convert currency.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: A tool-capable model that will not call tools fails the core function-calling task despite documenting the capability.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The numeric answer was right but not wrapped as the contract requires.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On word problems the model reasoned step by step to the exact correct figure and then stated it plainly instead of boxing it.
failure_analysis.example_quote: To find the final price of the jacket, we need to follow these steps:
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Correct work with the wrong final format scores zero under strict checking and breaks automated grading.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The answer was semantically right but wrapped in a code fence the contract forbids.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: Correct classification and extraction JSON came back surrounded by triple backticks on 5 cases.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Strict parsers reject these correct answers, so a fence-stripping step is required before scoring or serving.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The repaired code passed all hidden tests but the reported bug line was wrong.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On bug repair the model fixed every defect correctly yet named a line one position off, as in the BUG_LINE 5 below.
failure_analysis.example_quote:
```python
def total_upto(n):
    total = 0
    for i in range(n + 1):
        total += i
    return total
BUG_LINE: 5
```
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Code review tooling that points developers at the reported line will point at the wrong line.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: A tool-loop turn produced no JSON where the loop contract requires it.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On short tool loops one case returned an empty message with no call and no result object, stalling the loop.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: An empty turn gives the loop harness nothing to act on, so the task cannot progress.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The turn returned something, but not the result shape the loop contract specifies.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On short tool loops the model returned ad hoc values such as bare city-to-number maps instead of the required result object.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Free-form results cannot be reconciled with the loop state, so the whole chain fails validation.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: Generated code ran but failed at least one hidden test.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: The CSV parser below handled every case except fields with embedded quotes, failing exactly one of nine hidden tests.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Near-correct code that fails edge cases is the hardest kind to catch without the hidden-test suite.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The generated SQL did not execute against the database.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: The query below selected a customer name through an orders alias that has no name column, so the database rejected it.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: A query that cannot run returns no rows at all, making alias discipline the first thing to verify.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The tool loop ended with the store in the wrong state.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: On short tool loops the model produced no calls at all, leaving orders unmodified where a cancellation or update was required.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Silent inaction in a stateful loop looks like success to a casual reader but changes nothing.

strengths: Bug fixes were functionally perfect: all 8 submitted repairs passed every hidden test, showing genuine debugging skill.
Word-problem arithmetic was exact on all 10 scored cases with quality 1.0, and code generation passed most hidden tests at 0.957.
Template extraction reached 0.958 with clean structured output, among the best in this group.
Support routing decisions were right 15 of 20 times, showing solid policy comprehension when it emitted JSON.
weaknesses: Ignored the JSON output contract on its entire home RAG test: 16 of 16 prose answers with zero citations.
Wrote full letters instead of safety verdicts, exhausting the token budget in 11 of 16 safety cases.
Refused 10 of 15 function calls while claiming to have no tools, despite documenting tool capability.
Multi-turn tool loops never fully succeeded: states left wrong, results malformed, or turns empty.
use_when: Bug repair where hidden tests judge the code and a human checks the reported line (HOME-06 style).
Template extraction from long texts with clean structured output (HOME-12 style).
Code generation from a spec with a test suite to catch edge cases (HOME-14 style).
Word-problem arithmetic where a post step can extract the final number from prose (HOME-13 style).
avoid_when: Grounded question answering that requires citations and abstention, its home task, where it scored zero.
Safety classification with tight token budgets, where verbose roleplay crowds out the verdict.
Single-turn function calling without supervision, where it refuses most calls.
Multi-turn stateful tool loops, where no chain completed correctly.
hardware_fit: Cold load took 4.5 seconds with the model fully on the GPU, first token arrived in 0.23 seconds, and sustained generation ran at 70.7 tokens per second. Speed is not the issue on this card. The practical costs were behavioral: long unguided answers that burned token budgets, and five long-context tests ruled out by the 8192-token runtime limit.
bottom_line: Command-r7b:7b is the run's split personality: genuinely strong at fixing code, solving word problems, and extracting structure, yet it scored zero on the RAG task built for it by answering entirely in uncited prose. Use it for code and extraction with format checks; do not trust it to follow a citation or verdict contract unsupervised.

strengths: Reading comprehension is excellent when the budget holds: RAG answers were all factually right at quality 1.0 and long-context wiki QA was 4 of 4.
Safety verdicts were sound at 0.938 with 5 strict passes, showing reliable judgment on non-operational requests.
Solved 4 genuinely hard contest-math problems, proving real reasoning capability inside the verbosity.
Markdown conversion at 0.948 and extraction at 0.940 show strong document-handling skills.
weaknesses: Reasoning that cannot be switched off consumed the whole token budget in 40 cases, the dominant failure of the run.
Code generation and SQL were gutted by the same cause: 7 of 8 code cases and 8 of 12 SQL cases never produced an answer.
Tool use is effectively absent: textual pseudo-calls instead of native calls, and no successful multi-turn chain.
Correct answers routinely arrive fenced, costing strict credit in 27 cases across 6 tests.
use_when: Grounded question answering over supplied documents where a fence-stripping step normalizes output (HOME-03 style).
Long-context wiki question answering with generous token budgets (HOME-09 style).
Safety verdicts on user messages with lenient parsing (HOME-08 style).
HTML-to-Markdown conversion where near-identical wording is acceptable (HOME-19 style).
avoid_when: Token-budget-sensitive reasoning tasks such as contest math or optimization on this hardware, where most cases never finish thinking.
Code and SQL generation under fixed budgets, where unfinished reasoning means no answer at all.
Any tool-calling workflow, native or multi-turn, which never succeeded in this run.
Strict JSON pipelines without a fence-stripping pre-step.
hardware_fit: Cold load took 4.1 seconds with the model fully on the GPU and prompt processing ran at 2912 tokens per second, but sustained generation managed 72.1 tokens per second while reasoning without limit, so single cases ran for many minutes and still expired. On an 8 GB card with always-on reasoning, this model is impractical for heavy reasoning tasks: single cases ran up to about 6 minutes (351 s max in this run) and still expired inside thinking.
bottom_line: Deepseek-r1:8b thinks deeply and reads well, but on this hardware its unswitchable reasoning is a liability: 40 cases burned their full budget inside thought and scored zero. Where answers escaped quickly it was often excellent, yet for timed reasoning, code, or tool work it cannot be recommended on this setup.

profile.documented: A small chat model documented for text and tool use with no reasoning mode and a 32768-token documented context. The run configuration makes an activation system prompt mandatory for function calling and restricts its documented tool role to single turns, with greedy sampling at temperature 0.0.
profile.role_in_run: HOME-24 (Single-turn function calling) was designed around this model. That test issues one independent request per case, each naming a function and arguments the model must emit as a single native call.

overall.rating_basis: Mean semantic quality 0.433 from its single scored test, home-test quality 0.433, and an OK rate of 36.7 percent combine to a rating of 4.2, weakly supported by design since only one test was scored.

home_test.title: Single-turn function calling
home_test.analysis: All 30 cases ran with a three-way split: 11 correct, 11 refusals on cases that needed a call, and 8 attempts cut off mid-call. The correct cases were mostly rightful declines of out-of-scope requests, so the model is good at saying no and poor at saying yes: whenever a real call was needed it either refused or rambled past the token limit. For the single-turn calling task built for it, that is a weak result.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The model made no tool call on a case that required one.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: Faced with currency, discount, and booking requests, the model declined and listed a narrower menu of weather, ticket, scheduling, and travel tasks instead of calling.
failure_analysis.example_quote: I apologize, but I cannot assist with converting currency or calculating specific transaction amounts.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: A function-calling model that declines its own documented functions fails the task it was deployed to do.

failure_analysis.english_meaning: The response hit the token limit before finishing.
failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: When it did attempt calls, the model emitted verbose malformed call text with repeated and padded arguments until the budget ran out mid-call.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: A call that never completes cannot be parsed or executed, so the extra verbosity directly destroys task success.

strengths: Correctly declined 11 out-of-scope requests, showing it can recognize tasks outside its menu.
With only one scored test, no cross-task conclusion is possible, which is stated here instead of padded.
weaknesses: Refused 11 of the cases that genuinely required a call, often disclaiming functions it is documented to serve.
All 8 attempted calls were cut off mid-stream with malformed, padded, and repeated arguments.
No demonstrated ability to emit one clean native call with exact arguments in this run.
use_when: Gatekeeping prompts where the job is to decline out-of-scope requests politely (a subset of HOME-24 style).
Ultra-lightweight on-device triage where its 461-token-per-second speed matters more than call accuracy, with a larger model verifying.
avoid_when: Single-turn function calling that must actually emit the call, its home task, where it succeeded weakly at best.
Currency, discount, or booking calls specifically, which it repeatedly declined.
Any multi-turn tool dialogue, which is not a documented scenario for this model.
hardware_fit: Cold load took 2.2 seconds with the model fully on the GPU, first token arrived in 0.04 seconds, and sustained generation hit 461.0 tokens per second, by far the fastest in this group. Speed is outstanding on this card; the entire problem is behavioral, since the fastest wrong answer is still wrong.
bottom_line: Functiongemma:270m is the fastest model in this group and the weakest at its own job: it politely declines what it should call and mangles the calls it attempts. Useful as a cheap first-pass gatekeeper, not as a function caller, on this hardware.

profile.documented: A chat model documented for text, vision, and structured JSON output, with no reasoning mode and a 131072-token documented context, but no documented tool capability. Sampling used temperature 1.0, and the run configuration notes that part of the model runs on the CPU on 8 GB cards and that system text is merged into the first user turn.
profile.role_in_run: HOME-05 (Chart reading) was designed around this model. That test shows charts as images and asks for exact values and labels read from them.

overall.rating_basis: Mean semantic quality 0.834 across 16 scored tests, home-test quality 0.333, and an OK rate of 31.8 percent combine to a rating of 5.8.

home_test.title: Chart reading
home_test.analysis: On the chart task built for it the model read only 2 of 12 charts exactly right, misread 3 values or labels, and fenced 7 answers. The fences are cosmetic, but the 3 genuine misreads plus a clean-format wrong value show real perception errors, not just format habits. For a vision home test, 0.333 is a weak result that its strong text scores elsewhere cannot excuse.

strengths: Text comprehension is outstanding: quality 1.0 on RAG, extraction, word problems, and document understanding, and 0.986 on multilingual classification.
Bug repair was flawless at 8 of 8, and code generation reached 0.958, both well above the group.
OCR transcription hit 0.979 with 9 of 10 exact, showing vision works well for clean text images.
SQL at 0.882 with 8 of 12 matched shows practical database-querying ability.
weaknesses: Fences everything: 65 fenced correct answers across 8 tests, the heaviest format tax in this group.
Chart reading on its home test managed only 0.333 with genuine misreads, not just fences.
Constrained optimization failed all 4 cases with infeasible schedules full of violations.
Long-context log tracking never scored: 2 context overflows on the 16384-token runtime, a hard ceiling.
use_when: Bug repair and code generation where tests judge correctness (HOME-06 and HOME-14 style).
Multilingual classification, RAG answers, and extraction where a fence-stripping step normalizes output first.
OCR transcription of clean text images (HOME-23 style).
Text-to-SQL drafting with result verification before execution (HOME-20 style).
avoid_when: Chart reading that demands exact values, its home task, where it managed only 0.333.
Constrained scheduling with hard machine and precedence rules, where every proposal was infeasible.
Strict JSON pipelines with no post-processing, where fences void perfect content.
Tool-calling workflows of any kind, which are outside its documented capability.
hardware_fit: Cold load took 9.1 seconds, first token arrived in 0.80 seconds, and sustained generation ran at 10.0 tokens per second with part of the model on the CPU, since only about 61 percent fits on the 8 GB card. This is the slowest model in the group by a wide margin and the only partial offload here. The practical consequence is slow interactive use, though batch-tolerant work such as transcription and extraction remains viable.
bottom_line: Gemma3:12b is the group's best pure reader: near-perfect text scores across eight tests, flawless bug repair, and excellent OCR, all taxed heavily by an inveterate fencing habit. It is a strong pick for comprehension and extraction with format post-processing, but not for charts, scheduling, or anything needing speed on this card.
